facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s with no history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
presented to the emergency department with a headache for 2 weeks
vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19
Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection
severe pain on ocular motion
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, with extension of inflammation into the apex
Serum IgG4: 277 mg/dL (normal, <123 mg/dL)
Sinus Cultures: Positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive
Right-sided headache 1 week later and right vision loss 2 days prior to presentation

presented to the emergency department with a headache for 2 weeks
vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19
Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection
severe pain on ocular motion
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, with extension of inflammation into the apex
Serum IgG4: 277 mg/dL (normal, <123 mg/dL)

concepts.why: Elevated serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells support this diagnosis
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus support this diagnosis
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells support this diagnosis
Opacification of the sphenoid sinus and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus support this diagnosis
Opacification of the ethmoid sinus and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus support this diagnosis
Opacification of the maxillary sinus and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus support this diagnosis
Opacification of the frontal sinus and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus support this diagnosis
Elevated serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells support this diagnosis

rationales.F05: Highly suggestive of IgG4-related ophthalmic disease due to severe vision loss and orbital involvement
rationales.F08: Bony erosion and extension of inflammation into the orbital apex is highly suggestive of IgG4-related ophthalmic disease
rationales.F09: Elevated serum IgG4 levels are highly suggestive of IgG4-related disease
rationales.F11: Dense infiltrate of IgG4-positive plasma cells is highly suggestive of IgG4-related disease

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's vision loss, limited visual acuity, and severe pain on ocular motion, combined with elevated Serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG4-positive plasma cells, support IgG4-related ophthalmic disease as the most specific diagnosis.
